findings.title: The new downsize definition replaces the existing width/height API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature: this second definition of `self.downsize` replaces the definition immediately above it. Existing calls using `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` now raise ArgumentError, and calls with four arguments treat the height as `opts`, causing `optimize` to fail when it accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`. Preserve the existing width/height interface or explicitly dispatch between the two supported forms.

findings.title: Resizing uploaded GIFs discards animation even when animation is allowed
findings.body: The controller passes the multipart tempfile path to `OptimizedImage.downsize`, but `optimize` selects its animated implementation only when that path ends in `.gif`. Multipart tempfile paths generally do not retain the uploaded filename extension, so even with `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled an oversized animated GIF goes through `convert` with the `[0]` frame selector. Because the conversion overwrites the upload itself, the remaining animation frames are permanently discarded. Select the animated processing path using the actual image format or original filename rather than the temporary path suffix.

findings.title: Keep the configured size limit for non-image attachments
findings.body: The fixed 10 MB validation limit applies to attachments as well as images, although the new server-side downsizing only handles images. Attachments exceeding `max_attachment_size_kb` now pass client validation and are uploaded only to be rejected by the server; conversely, sites configured to allow attachments larger than 10 MB can no longer upload them through this client. Apply the relaxed limit only to images and retain the configured attachment limit.
